title: Projective prime-to-ell log-smooth alteration over a trait
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Use fs log structures, charts and log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The canonical log structure on a trait is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on its generic point; a uniformizer gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$. In this statement, log smooth over that trait has its fs chart meaning: etale locally on source and target there are compatible charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, the group map injective with torsion in its cokernel of finite order invertible on the source, such that the induced scheme map to $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ is smooth. Here $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on $P$ with multiplication induced by the monoid law.

Let $S$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $X$ be an integral regular scheme, flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means that $X$ admits a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_S$. There are a finite dominant extension of traits $T\to S$, an integral regular scheme $Y$ quasi-projective of finite type over $T$ and over $S$, an fs log structure $M_Y$ making $(Y,M_Y)\to T$ log smooth for the canonical trait log structure, and a projective dominant $S$-morphism $f:Y\to X$ that is generically finite etale of positive degree $d$ not divisible by $\ell$. Here projective means factoring as a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_X$ followed by projection, and generically finite etale means finite etale over a nonempty open of $X$, with $[k(Y):k(X)]=d$. No purity conclusion is included.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-trait-semistable-galois-alteration] to $X/S$. Obtain $G$, $S^{\prime}$, the semistable $X^{\prime}$, and the projective map $a:X^{\prime}\to X$. Keep the nonempty open $U\subset X$ where $E=a^{-1}U\to U$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor. The log structure on $X^{\prime}$ is log regular and log smooth over $S^{\prime}$. The constant-field normalization mentioned at the beginning of XVI 3.7 is included in this semistable input; no arbitrary finite extension is composed with the eventual alteration of $X$.

source.place: XVI 3.7, first two paragraphs and four bullets, p.254.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index], choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $H\le G$; write $\#H=\ell^a$ and $d=[G:H]$, so $\ell\nmid d$. Apply [lem-per-tame-trait-quotient-log-etale] to $S^{\prime}/S$ and $H$. Its order is a unit because $\ell$ is a unit on $S$. This gives a finite dominant complete strictly henselian trait $T\to S$ and makes $X^{\prime}\to T$ log smooth. The action of $H$ on $T$ is trivial by the definition of the invariant ring. The degree of $S^{\prime}/T$ need only divide $\#H$, since $H$ need not act faithfully on the trait.

source.place: XVI 3.7, definition of H and T and the log-etale trait extension, p.254.

proof.text: The finite map $T\to S$ is separated: on an affine chart its diagonal is the closed immersion given by the surjection $B\otimes_R B\to B$, $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$. For any $S$-scheme $V$ mapping to $T$, its graph into $V\times_S T$ is therefore closed: it is a base change of that diagonal, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. If $V$ is quasi-projective over $S$, pull its locally closed embedding into $\mathbf P^n_S$ back to $T$ and compose with this graph to obtain a locally closed embedding $V\to\mathbf P^n_T$. Apply this to $X^{\prime}$. It is of finite type over $T$: on affine charts, generators of its coordinate algebra over $R$ also generate it over the intervening finite $R$-algebra $B$; quasi-compactness follows from its finite-type $S$-structure. Thus $X^{\prime}$ is quasi-projective of finite type over $T$.

source.place: XVI 3.7, hypotheses of the relative equivariant modification, p.254; elementary graph argument.

proof.text: Every geometric-point stabilizer for $H$ has order dividing $\ell^a$. Residue characteristics on an $S$-scheme are either zero or the residue characteristic $p\ne\ell$, so the action is tame. The torsor on $U$ makes it generically free. All hypotheses of [lem-per-gabber-log-smooth-equivariant-modification] hold for $X^{\prime}\to T$: log regularity comes from Step 1 and log smoothness from Step 2, and Step 3 supplies quasi-projectivity and finite type. Obtain an $H$-equivariant projective birational $h:W\to X^{\prime}$ with $W$ integral and quasi-projective over $T$, and $Q=W/H$ fs log regular and log smooth over $T$. This uses the relative log-smooth theorem, rather than an absolute modification theorem which would not assert preservation of relative log smoothness.

source.place: XVI 3.7, equivariant resolution and quotient, p.254; X Theorem 1.1, p.136.

proof.text: The composite $W\xrightarrow h X^{\prime}\xrightarrow a X$ is projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. Apply [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] first over $T$ and then over $X$. Its base hypotheses hold: $T$ is affine Noetherian and $X$ is Noetherian quasi-projective over the affine trait $S$. These applications identify the same quotient, by its categorical uniqueness. They give that $Q$ is integral and quasi-projective of finite type over $T$, and that $q:Q\to X$ is projective. The quotient map $W\to Q$ is finite surjective. Since $W\to X$ is dominant, so is $q$. Here $X$ is locally Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme] and quasi-compact by its finite-type map to affine $S$, hence Noetherian.

source.place: XVI 3.7, quotient X double-prime/H and projective map to X, pp.254--255; finite-quotient projectivity as in Rydh 4.4, 4.7, 4.9.

proof.text: The ring of $T$ is complete Noetherian local, hence excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Apply [lem-per-log-regular-projective-log-resolution] to $Q$ over this excellent affine base. Step 5 gives integrality, quasi-projectivity and finite type, and Step 4 gives its fs log regularity. Obtain $b:(Y,M_Y)\to Q$ projective birational with $Y$ integral regular. The same theorem, applied to the log-smooth $Q\to T$, makes $Y\to T$ log smooth in the sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Since $Y$ is regular, hence locally Noetherian, [lem-per-trait-log-smooth-uniformizer-chart] applied to $(Y,M_Y)\to T$ and a uniformizer of $T$ gives, etale locally on $Y$, charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, $u^{\rm gp}$ injective, the torsion of its cokernel finite of order invertible on $Y$, and $Y\to T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ smooth. This is exactly the fs chart meaning of log smoothness over the trait $T$ fixed in the statement. Set $f=q\circ b:Y\to X$. It is projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] and dominant because both maps are dominant.

source.place: XVI 3.7, last geometric resolution before the purity application, pp.254--255; VIII 3.4.9.

proof.text: Shrink $U$ so that $h$ is an isomorphism above $E=a^{-1}U$. Intersect the finitely many $H$-translates of a dense isomorphism open in $X^{\prime}$, and call its closed complement $C$. The projective map $a$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], so $a(C)$ is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It misses the generic point: the generic fibre of $a$ is the single generic point of integral $X^{\prime}$, which is in the isomorphism open. Remove $a(C)$ from $U$. Since $h$ is an $H$-equivariant isomorphism above $E$, the $H$-invariant open $h^{-1}E\subset W$ is $E$ with the restricted $H$-action. The quotient restriction in [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] identifies $q^{-1}U$ with the quotient $\pi:E\to E/H$ of this restricted action, which is finite, has $\mathcal O_{E/H}=(\pi_*\mathcal O_E)^H$ and is categorical. By [lem-per-torsor-subgroup-quotient-finite-etale], applied to the connected Galois cover $E\to U$ with group $G$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois] and the subgroup $H$, the map $q^{-1}U=E/H\to U$ is a connected finite etale cover all of whose geometric fibres have $d=[G:H]$ points. No normality of $H$ is required.

source.place: XVI 3.7, prime-to-ell generic degree, pp.254--255; expand the subgroup quotient on the original G-torsor.

proof.text: Let $D\subset Q$ be the closed complement of a dense open where $b$ is an isomorphism. Since $q$ is projective, it is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], and $q(D)$ is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Over the open from Step 7, the generic fibre of $Q\to X$ is the single generic point of the integral finite etale cover. It is outside $D$, so $q(D)$ misses the generic point of $X$. Remove $q(D)$ from $U$. Now $f^{-1}U\to U$ is that same finite etale cover of degree $d>0$ prime to $\ell$; in particular $[k(Y):k(X)]=d$. Finally write $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_X$ for the projective factorization of $f$ and $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ for the given locally closed embedding. Their product followed by [lem-chow-segre] embeds $Y$ locally closed in $\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_S$. The analogous construction using $b$ and the embedding of $Q$ over $T$ proves quasi-projectivity over $T$. Projective maps are finite type by properness; [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] gives finite type over $S$ and over $T$. These are every clause of the required geometric alteration.

source.place: XVI 3.7, conclusion of the geometric construction, p.255; elementary shrinking and projective embeddings, using the cited general geometry.

proof_origin.place: Expose XVI 3.7, pp.254--255, geometric construction only; intermediate theorems X 1.1 and VIII 3.4.9 and elementary open shrinking made explicit.
